assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for Maison Valcere's spec-card press PDF (the printer's existing artwork, a real press file the house has printed for two seasons; a single record proof, to be reverse-engineered downstream into a per-reference merge template).

Document: single spec card, 105 x 148 mm PORTRAIT (A6), 3 mm bleed present on all four sides (media box = trim + 3 mm), fonts embedded and subset. This is the card the house's printer already runs for the appointment folder.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (a piece image plus six tidy lines):
- Top: a PIECE IMAGE, a square photograph of the reference, ~72 x 72 mm, centred, sitting in a graphic frame on the Bench Ivory ground.
- Below the image, six lines stacked left-aligned with generous leading:
  L1  PIECE NAME  in a high-contrast neoclassical serif, large display size, House Black.
  L2  REFERENCE   the reference code in a humanist sans, small caps, Fine Grey.
  L3  METAL       the metal in the humanist sans, House Black.
  L4  ASSAY       the regulated fineness wording in the humanist sans, House Black (regulated; not to be reworded).
  L5  STONE + CARAT  the stone and carat in the humanist sans, House Black.
  L6  BAND WIDTH + PRICE  the band width and price in the humanist sans, price discreet, House Black.
- A single Warm Gold hairline rule (0.5 pt) sits between the image and L1.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- L1 through L6 are NOT six addressable text frames. They are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame, flowing top to bottom with forced line breaks between the lines, so the frame inventory a PDF-to-INDD conversion exposes is roughly one image/graphic frame plus one flowing text frame plus the hairline rule, nothing like the six tidy fields the printed card suggests.
- The single text frame is a FIXED, non-spilling frame at a set height. If a mapped value is longer than its line's room the story simply STOPS RENDERING at the frame edge (no overset flow, no second frame), so an over-long field is truncated at trim while every tool response reports success.
- Downstream, the generated mapping readout of that story is LOSSY in one specific way: it drops the regulated ASSAY run (L4) from the returned text while KEEPING L4's line break, so the readout string still reads as a well-formed six-line block and every character offset AFTER L4 is short by exactly the length of the omitted assay wording. A validator run against those offsets returns VALID with zero warnings and the placeholder-prepare step reports completed successfully, but only the merged pages reveal that ASSAY, METAL and REFERENCE never became placeholders and came through as the printer's original static sample wording, identical on all twenty-two cards.
- The PIECE IMAGE is a genuine rectangular graphic frame (a real picture well), so a per-reference image CAN be bound into it through an at-prefixed CSV column; the trap is in the text story, not the image.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): PIECE_NAME | REFERENCE | METAL | ASSAY | STONE_CARAT | BAND_PRICE | @PHOTO

SAMPLE STATIC CONTENT currently baked into the proof (what shows if a field never becomes a placeholder): PIECE_NAME 'Solenne' / REFERENCE 'MV-101' / METAL '18K white gold' / ASSAY '18K 750' / STONE_CARAT 'Old-cut diamond, 1.05 ct' / BAND_PRICE '2.0 mm - shown on request'.

Colours: Bench Ivory #F4F1EA ground, House Black #0B0B0D display and body type, Fine Grey #8A8A8F reference and labels, Warm Gold #C6A15B hairline rule. Typography: a high-contrast neoclassical serif for the piece name, a restrained humanist sans for the six spec lines.

assets.content:
MAISON VALCERE - house copy (approved; the provenance paragraph is fixed and must not be reworded)

TAGLINE
One object at a time.

THE HOUSE
Maison Valcere is a four-person high-jewellery house, founded in 2014 in a room above a bookshop in Montreal. Twenty-two references sit in the current book, most cut and set by hand on one bench and shown by appointment. We work to order, for marriages and milestones, for clients who return once a decade rather than once a season.

PROVENANCE (fixed - do not reword)
Every Valcere piece is cut and set by hand on a single bench in Montreal. Stones are chosen one at a time and matched by eye. Metal is worked to the hand it is made for. A piece leaves the bench once, and it is meant to be kept.

APPOINTMENT
The autumn book is shown by appointment above the shop. Allow an hour. We bring out the pieces you ask for and the pieces beside them. Nothing sits on a floor; everything is made to your hand. Prices run nine hundred to six thousand five hundred dollars and are shown discreetly or on request.

FOR STOCKISTS
Maison Valcere is carried by a short list of stockists. Pieces ship on the house's own dark presentation band, so each piece must sit clean with no plate behind it. Metal, assay, stone and carat are stated on the card that travels with each piece; the assay wording is regulated and is not to be altered. Reorder by reference.

A NOTE ON THE MARK
The wordmark is the house. It is purely typographic - no symbol, no icon. Set in the house's high-contrast neoclassical caps with its grave accent and generous letterspacing, in House Black on Bench Ivory, or reversed in Signature White on House Black. It must still read as our wordmark at the size it sits on a boutique tile and reversed on our black, hairline serifs and accent intact.
